phases.name: Detect and correlate
phases.description: Ingest monitoring signals durably, remove duplicate alerts, score related alerts, and guard the two-minute detection path.

phases.name: Persist incidents and calculate impact
phases.description: Create one incident lifecycle and use a versioned service dependency graph to estimate blast radius.

phases.name: Route and secure response
phases.description: Resolve ownership, notify the active on-call team, capture acknowledgements, and authorize responder access.

phases.name: Recommend and control remediation
phases.description: Retrieve past resolutions, suggest runbooks, and execute only approved actions with bounded retries.

phases.name: Measure, report, and learn
phases.description: Track lifecycle metrics, generate post-incident reports, and promote reviewed incident outcomes into model training.

steps.title: Set measurable incident and alert contracts
steps.content: Assumption: this walkthrough serves multiple organizations; for a single-organization deployment, the tenant boundary can be omitted. Treat each alert as a timestamped, organization- and service-scoped signal with event ID, environment, severity, source, and trace link. Define detected_at as creation of the first actionable incident after the first qualifying signal; the brief's target is within 2 minutes end to end, including ingestion and correlation lag. Report the latency distribution and every miss, without inventing a percentile threshold. Validate correlation accuracy above 90% on labeled incident groups, handle 10k+ alerts per hour, and measure 80% alert-noise reduction against a labeled baseline without suppressing distinct critical incidents. These are acceptance targets, not assumed outcomes; the brief does not specify burst rate or component sizing.

steps.title: Add monitoring signal sources
steps.content: Collect health metrics, traces, logs, and alert events from the fleet; retain source timestamps and service identity so detection can be audited.

component.label: Fleet Monitoring Signals
component.description: Timestamped service health and alert sources

properties.purpose: Collect timestamped metrics, traces, logs, and health alerts with stable service IDs and source event IDs across the microservice fleet.

component.highlightReason: The detector needs attributable source signals and a measurable first-signal timestamp.

steps.title: Add durable alert ingestion
steps.content: Partition by tenant and service under the multi-organization assumption, preserve event IDs, and replay after processor failure. Load-test the stated 10k+ alerts per hour; test bursts separately without treating an unspecified burst rate or retention duration as a requirement.

component.label: Durable Alert Bus

properties.purpose: Accept the stated 10k+ alerts per hour, partition by tenant/service under the multi-organization assumption, retain event IDs for replay, and isolate ingestion from downstream correlation.

component.highlightReason: A durable buffer prevents transient downstream failures from dropping qualifying signals.

steps.title: Publish signals to the alert bus
steps.content: Publish authenticated, schema-validated alert events with event time and service identity; acknowledge only after the broker has stored them.

connection.label: Alert events
connection.description: Durable, authenticated event-time signal publication with stable event IDs.

steps.title: Add stateful signal processing
steps.content: Normalize alerts, hold short event-time windows, deduplicate retransmissions, and maintain bounded correlation state. Load-test against the stated 10k+ alerts per hour and the two-minute end-to-end detection target; size the processor from measured event mix and burst behavior instead of assuming an events-per-second rate.

component.label: Alert Normalizer and Correlator

properties.purpose: Normalize alerts, deduplicate by event ID and short-lived service/severity fingerprints, maintain event-time windows, and emit incident candidates with source evidence.

component.highlightReason: The windowed processor makes incident detection timely and replayable.

steps.title: Consume the alert stream
steps.content: Consume partitioned alerts with checkpointed offsets and backpressure; preserve original event times across replay.

connection.label: Raw alerts
connection.description: Checkpointed consumption of tenant/service-partitioned alerts with event-time metadata.

steps.title: Choose bounded deduplication before grouping
steps.content: Use exact event-ID idempotency first, then a short-lived similarity fingerprint within tenant, service, and severity. Keep originals and suppressed counts for audit. Measure 80% noise reduction against a labeled replay set while separately checking that no distinct high-severity incident was hidden.

decision.question: How should repeated alerts be suppressed without hiding new incidents?
decision.chosen: Exact ID deduplication plus bounded, scoped similarity fingerprints
decision.chosenReason: It removes retransmissions and near-duplicates while preserving evidence and a safety check for distinct critical incidents.

alternatives.tradeoff: Reduces volume but can merge unrelated services, tenants, or severity changes.
Preserves raw signals but cannot meet the noise-reduction target.

properties.purpose: Deduplicate exact event IDs and short-lived tenant/service/severity fingerprints; retain original evidence and suppressed counts; validate 80% noise reduction without losing distinct critical incidents.

steps.title: Add correlation and anomaly inference
steps.content: Score candidate alert groups using service, topology, temporal, and trace features; return model version and confidence, never an unexplained binary merge. This component produces scores; the separate validation gate determines whether correlation accuracy meets the brief.

component.label: Incident Correlation Inference

properties.purpose: Score anomaly and correlation candidates with model version, confidence, service/topology features, and bounded inference latency; expose a rules fallback.

component.highlightReason: A versioned scorer can distinguish related alerts while keeping model decisions inspectable.

steps.title: Send candidates for scoring
steps.content: Send bounded candidate windows and features rather than all raw telemetry; enforce an inference deadline inside the two-minute detection budget.

connection.label: Candidate features
connection.description: Deadline-bound scoring request with tenant, service, time window, and topology features.

steps.title: Return explainable scores
steps.content: Return cluster score, confidence, and model version; if inference times out, the processor uses conservative rule-based grouping and flags uncertainty. The response is evidence for the separate accuracy evaluation, not proof that its target has been met.

connection.label: Score and confidence
connection.description: Versioned score response with deadline and conservative timeout fallback.

steps.title: Choose a measured correlation gate
steps.content: Evaluate correlation accuracy above 90% on a held-out, incident-level labeled set across services and noisy periods. Inspect false merges separately because joining two real incidents is more dangerous than leaving two alerts ungrouped. Shadow-test new model versions and fall back to conservative rules on timeout or drift.

decision.question: When may model scores merge alerts into a single incident?
decision.chosen: Versioned confidence gate validated above 90% correlation accuracy with false-merge review
decision.chosenReason: A labeled release gate and rules fallback make model quality and failure behavior explicit.

alternatives.option: Merge on a fixed message similarity threshold
alternatives.tradeoff: Fast but misses topology context and can merge independent incidents.
Hides false merges and loses a measurable release criterion.

properties.purpose: Versioned correlation scoring; release only after held-out incident-level accuracy above 90% and false-merge review; shadow-test and fall back to conservative rules on timeout or drift.

steps.title: Scale before detection lag breaks the budget
steps.content: Measure broker oldest-event age, checkpoint lag, inference p95, and end-to-end detection age under 10k+ alerts per hour and bursts. Exercise broker replay and model outage in the load test.

scaleTrigger.metric: Oldest unprocessed alert age approaches the 2-minute detection budget during 10k+ alerts/hour load
scaleTrigger.action: Increase broker partitions and processor replicas, reserve inference capacity, and shed noncritical enrichment before core detection
scaleTrigger.impact: Keeps qualifying incident creation timely while retaining durable replay; promotion requires measured detection within 2 minutes for qualifying signals under the agreed load.

steps.title: Add the incident lifecycle service
steps.content: Create one incident per accepted correlated group with first_signal_at, detected_at, acknowledged_at, resolved_at, status, source alert IDs, and immutable transitions. Idempotency prevents replay from opening duplicate incidents.

component.label: Incident Lifecycle Service
component.description: Idempotent incident creation and state transitions

properties.purpose: Own incident IDs, first-signal/detection/acknowledgement/resolution timestamps, deduplicated alert membership, status transitions, audit events, and responder approvals.

component.highlightReason: One lifecycle owner anchors routing, metrics, remediation, and reports to the same incident.

steps.title: Open or update incidents from candidate groups
steps.content: Use an idempotency key derived from tenant, group, and window; update an existing incident when late alerts belong to it instead of creating a second page.

connection.label: Incident candidates
connection.description: Idempotent candidate upsert with source IDs, event time, evidence, and correlation confidence.

steps.title: Add the incident system of record
steps.content: Persist incident state, evidence pointers, ownership, acknowledgement, resolution, approvals, and an immutable audit trail. Use multi-zone replication and point-in-time recovery for the authoritative record.

component.label: Incident and Resolution Store

properties.purpose: Store incident transitions, alert evidence references, on-call acknowledgements, approved runbook outcomes, and reviewed resolution labels for reports and learning.

component.highlightReason: Durable, auditable incident history is required for metrics, reports, and safe feedback.

steps.title: Persist lifecycle transitions
steps.content: Write state transitions and an outbox record atomically, so retries of routing and report jobs cannot lose or duplicate incident changes.

connection.label: Incident state and outbox
connection.description: Transactional state, timestamps, evidence links, approval audit, and outbox events.

steps.title: Add a versioned service dependency graph
steps.content: Store service-to-service dependencies and ownership for 100+ microservices, with environment, edge type, discovery timestamp, and graph version. Ingest topology from service inventory or traces; reject stale or cross-tenant edges.

component.label: Service Dependency Graph

properties.purpose: Maintain a versioned, tenant-scoped dependency graph for 100+ microservices with discovery time, environment, service ownership, and edge confidence.

component.highlightReason: Blast-radius analysis needs explicit service dependencies rather than a flat alert list.

steps.title: Add bounded blast-radius analysis
steps.content: Traverse upstream consumers and downstream dependencies from impacted services, stop at bounded depth, and return affected service IDs, confidence, graph version, and uncertainty.

component.label: Blast-Radius Analyzer
component.description: Bounded dependency traversal and impact ranking

properties.purpose: Traverse versioned dependencies for 100+ microservices with cycle guards and a bounded depth; rank affected services and expose stale-topology uncertainty.

component.highlightReason: Impact ranking turns a service alert into an actionable affected-service view.

steps.title: Request an impact estimate
steps.content: Pass incident ID, service IDs, environment, and observed symptoms; use a deadline so slow graph queries cannot block incident creation or paging.

connection.label: Affected-service request
connection.description: Deadline-bound blast-radius request; incident creation proceeds if analysis is unavailable.

steps.title: Query the dependency graph
steps.content: Read a versioned, tenant-scoped snapshot and bound breadth, depth, and traversal time across 100+ microservices.

connection.label: Versioned dependencies
connection.description: Bounded, cycle-safe traversal with tenant and environment filters.

steps.title: Attach the impact estimate
steps.content: Return affected services and topology version for routing and the incident timeline; mark an estimate provisional when topology is stale.

connection.label: Blast radius and confidence
connection.description: Affected services, graph version, confidence, and stale-data marker.

steps.title: Choose bounded traversal with stale-data disclosure
steps.content: For 100+ microservices, traverse only relevant dependencies with cycle guards and a deadline. Keep the last known graph version for partial results, but display staleness and page the directly affected owner when topology cannot be trusted.

decision.question: How should blast-radius analysis behave when topology is large or stale?
decision.chosen: Bounded, versioned traversal with explicit uncertainty and direct-owner fallback
decision.chosenReason: It keeps incident response moving without presenting stale reachability as fact.

alternatives.tradeoff: Can delay paging and amplify cycles or hot graph reads.

alternatives.option: Assume every connected service is affected
alternatives.tradeoff: Overstates impact and sends noisy pages.

properties.purpose: Bounded, cycle-safe traversal of a versioned graph for 100+ microservices; return affected services, confidence, and staleness; fall back to the direct service owner on graph timeout.

steps.title: Keep detection independent of enrichment failures
steps.content: A failed graph lookup or model endpoint must not prevent a high-confidence monitoring signal from opening a provisional incident. Store the missing-enrichment reason, retry asynchronously, and show responders which conclusions are provisional. Replay uses stable IDs so late enrichment updates the same incident.

steps.title: Add on-call routing and escalation
steps.content: Resolve current team by directly affected service, environment, ownership version, and active rota; derive secondary teams from blast radius. Persist page, escalation, acknowledgement, and handoff timestamps.

component.label: On-Call Routing Service
component.description: Owner lookup, schedule, escalation, and acknowledgement

properties.purpose: Route to the active owner of the directly affected service, escalate after an acknowledgement deadline, and record page/ack/handoff events with rota version.

component.highlightReason: A correlated incident needs an accountable responder, not merely an alert count.

steps.title: Send incidents to the owner resolver
steps.content: Include incident severity, direct service, affected services, topology confidence, and dedupe key; avoid paging every downstream team by default.

connection.label: Route or escalate
connection.description: Idempotent incident route request with direct owner and affected-service context.

steps.title: Add responder notifications
steps.content: Deliver pages through configured channels with provider retries and delivery receipts; escalation uses acknowledgement, not a send API success, as its stop condition.

component.label: Responder Paging

properties.purpose: Send idempotent on-call pages through push, email, and SMS; return delivery receipts and retry failed channels while escalation waits for human acknowledgement.

component.highlightReason: Pages must reach the selected team and expose delivery failure.

steps.title: Page the active on-call contact
steps.content: Send deduplicated pages with incident ID, severity, service, and runbook link; retry delivery by channel without creating duplicate incident notifications.

connection.label: On-call page
connection.description: Idempotent multi-channel page with selected team and escalation tier.

steps.title: Capture delivery and acknowledgement events
steps.content: Record page delivery and authenticated responder acknowledgement against the incident; use acknowledgement to calculate MTTA and stop further escalation.

connection.label: Page and acknowledgement receipts
connection.description: Signed receipt and acknowledgement events keyed by incident and responder identity.

steps.title: Persist the routing audit
steps.content: Store owner, rota version, page attempts, handoffs, and escalation deadlines so MTTA and routing failures can be reconstructed.

connection.label: Owner and escalation audit
connection.description: Durable route, page, acknowledgement, and escalation records.

steps.title: Add the responder console
steps.content: Show the incident timeline, source evidence, impacted services, confidence, current owner, and proposed remediation; require explicit responder actions for acknowledgement and approvals.

component.label: Responder Console
component.description: Authenticated incident triage and approval surface

properties.purpose: Display incident evidence, blast radius and uncertainty, on-call state, historical suggestions, and explicit approve/reject controls for runbooks.

component.highlightReason: Responders need one place to inspect evidence and make accountable decisions.

steps.title: Connect the responder console
steps.content: Use authenticated HTTPS for incident details, acknowledgements, comments, and runbook approvals; never trust a client-supplied team or incident role.

connection.label: Incident response API
connection.description: Authenticated triage, acknowledgement, and approval requests with server-side authorization.

steps.title: Add responder identity and policy
steps.content: Authorize tenant, incident, team, and action scopes under the multi-organization assumption; require MFA for privileged remediation and log approval identity without storing secrets in incident text.

component.label: Responder Identity and Policy

properties.purpose: Enforce tenant, incident, team, and action scopes for responders; require MFA for privileged runbook approval and audit actor identity.

component.highlightReason: Incident data and remediation privileges cross a security boundary.

steps.title: Authorize incident actions
steps.content: The incident service checks actor, tenant, team, incident, and approval scopes before returning sensitive data or accepting state changes.

connection.label: Policy decision
connection.description: Server-side responder and incident-scope authorization; audit denials.

steps.title: Choose direct-owner paging before secondary fanout
steps.content: Page the direct service owner first, include affected teams as context, and escalate if no authenticated acknowledgement arrives by the incident's severity deadline. If ownership is missing, page a defined platform fallback and flag the ownership gap for correction.

decision.question: Who should receive the initial page for a multi-service incident?
decision.chosen: Direct owner first, severity-timed escalation, then targeted secondary teams
decision.chosenReason: It preserves a clear accountable responder and avoids paging every possibly affected team.

alternatives.tradeoff: Fast fanout but creates alert noise and ambiguous ownership.

alternatives.option: Wait until blast radius is complete
alternatives.tradeoff: A stale graph could delay acknowledgement.

properties.purpose: Page the direct service owner using a versioned rota; escalate by severity until an authenticated acknowledgement, then notify targeted secondary teams. Use a platform fallback when ownership is missing and persist every handoff.

steps.title: Add a reviewed resolution index
steps.content: Index only resolved incidents with reviewed cause, service, symptoms, runbook outcome, and source links. Filter retrieval by tenant and service under the multi-organization assumption before similarity scoring; do not treat an unreviewed postmortem as an approved action.

component.label: Reviewed Resolution Index

properties.purpose: Index reviewed incident summaries and successful remediation outcomes with tenant/service filters, source links, and approval state; remove superseded guidance.

component.highlightReason: Suggestions need traceable historical cases instead of free-form guesses.

steps.title: Add the remediation recommender
steps.content: Rank similar reviewed incidents and runbooks, attach evidence links and confidence, and show prerequisites and risk. A low-confidence suggestion remains a search result, not an executable instruction.

component.label: Remediation Recommender

properties.purpose: Retrieve tenant/service-filtered reviewed resolutions, rank by symptom and topology match, cite source incidents, and present confidence, prerequisites, and risk to responders.

component.highlightReason: The brief requires suggestions grounded in prior resolutions.

steps.title: Request remediation suggestions
steps.content: Send only scoped incident symptoms, affected services, and evidence pointers; keep suggestions asynchronous so retrieval failure cannot block paging.

connection.label: Suggestion request
connection.description: Scoped incident context for evidence-linked, nonblocking remediation suggestions.

steps.title: Retrieve reviewed resolutions
steps.content: Filter by tenant and service, then rank similar symptoms; include source incident IDs and review status in every result.

connection.label: Similar resolved cases
connection.description: Tenant/service-filtered similarity retrieval with reviewed source references.

steps.title: Index completed reviewed cases
steps.content: After resolution review, publish a versioned summary and verified outcome to the index; remove or reindex stale entries when a runbook is revoked.

connection.label: Reviewed outcomes
connection.description: Versioned reviewed resolution summaries, labels, and revocations for retrieval.

steps.title: Add a durable runbook task queue
steps.content: Queue only explicitly approved, scoped runbook tasks with incident ID, approval ID, idempotency key, expiry, and a bounded retry policy; dead-letter exhausted tasks for human review. Set timeout and retry values from operational policy rather than treating them as brief requirements.

component.label: Approved Runbook Queue

properties.purpose: Hold only approved, incident-scoped runbook tasks with idempotency, expiry, bounded retries, and dead-letter review.

component.highlightReason: Remediation execution needs a durable approval boundary and controlled retry path.

steps.title: Queue approved runbooks
steps.content: The recommender proposes; the incident service queues a task only after server-verified responder approval. The message carries an incident-scoped approval ID rather than a reusable credential.

connection.label: Approved runbook task
connection.description: Incident-scoped task emitted by the lifecycle service only after server-verified human approval.

steps.title: Add constrained runbook execution
steps.content: Execute allowlisted, reversible actions first; check approval and expiry, use short-lived scoped credentials, record before/after evidence, and stop on unknown state.

component.label: Runbook Executor

properties.purpose: Execute allowlisted, incident-scoped runbooks only after approval and expiry checks; use idempotency keys, short-lived credentials, bounded retries, and before/after audit evidence.

component.highlightReason: Suggestions become safe actions only through an explicit responder-controlled execution path.

steps.title: Consume approved tasks
steps.content: Workers claim expiring tasks with visibility timeouts; duplicates are harmless because the action uses the incident/runbook idempotency key.

connection.label: Scoped runbook task
connection.description: At-least-once delivery with expiry, idempotency key, and dead-letter handling.

steps.title: Record remediation results
steps.content: Report attempt, approval, before/after observations, success or failure, and rollback outcome to the incident timeline. Do not auto-resolve solely because a runbook API returned success.

connection.label: Execution outcome
connection.description: Auditable result and rollback evidence linked to incident and approval ID.

steps.title: Choose human approval for runbook execution
steps.content: Start with suggestions and allowlisted reversible runbooks. A qualified responder explicitly approves an incident-scoped action; the worker rechecks policy, expiry, and current state. Destructive or ambiguous actions remain manual.

decision.question: Should a high-confidence suggestion execute automatically?
decision.chosen: Require scoped human approval, then execute only allowlisted reversible runbooks
decision.chosenReason: Similarity confidence does not prove the current environment is safe for an automated change.

alternatives.tradeoff: Can amplify an incorrect diagnosis or act on stale incident context.
Safer initially but loses repeatable remediation for reviewed low-risk cases.

properties.purpose: Execute only allowlisted reversible runbooks after incident-scoped human approval, current-state and expiry checks, scoped credentials, idempotency, audit, and bounded rollback; leave destructive actions manual.

steps.title: Choose evidence-linked suggestions over opaque answers
steps.content: Rank retrieved reviewed cases, show source links and outcome confidence, and abstain when no sufficiently similar case exists. Keep the responder's final diagnosis and rejected suggestions for later review.

decision.question: How should historical resolutions become suggestions?
decision.chosen: Filtered retrieval with cited cases, confidence, and abstention
decision.chosenReason: Responders can verify relevance and avoid ungrounded remediation claims.

alternatives.option: Generate a free-form instruction without sources
alternatives.tradeoff: May invent unsafe actions and cannot be audited against prior outcomes.

alternatives.option: Always show the most similar case
alternatives.tradeoff: Even a poor match appears authoritative when evidence is weak.

properties.purpose: Retrieve reviewed tenant/service-matched cases, cite prior outcomes, rank by symptoms and dependency context, expose confidence and prerequisites, and abstain when evidence is weak.

steps.title: Recheck worker authorization
steps.content: The worker verifies the approval actor, tenant, incident, action scope, and short-lived grant at execution time; revoked approval prevents a queued task from running.

connection.label: Execution grant
connection.description: Short-lived, incident-scoped authorization and revocation check before runbook action.

steps.title: Scale the worker pool without unsafe retries
steps.content: Observe queue oldest-task age, dead-letter count, approval expiry, and worker failures. Scale workers on backlog only while policy checks and downstream limits continue to hold.

scaleTrigger.metric: Approved runbook queue age exceeds the operator-configured response target, or dead-letter volume rises; the brief specifies no runbook execution deadline
scaleTrigger.action: Increase bounded worker concurrency, rate-limit downstream systems, inspect failures, and keep expired approvals in a human-review queue
scaleTrigger.impact: Improves execution delay without turning retries into duplicate or unauthorized changes.

steps.title: Add incident lifecycle analytics
steps.content: Define metric boundaries consistently: MTTD from the first qualifying signal to incident detection, MTTA from the first page to authenticated acknowledgement, and MTTR from detection to verified resolution. Segment by service and severity; show the latency distribution and missing timestamps as well as averages, without adding percentile SLOs absent from the brief.

component.label: Incident Lifecycle Metrics
component.description: MTTD, MTTA, MTTR, and noise-reduction evidence

properties.purpose: Measure MTTD, MTTA, MTTR, correlation accuracy, suppression ratio, false merges, queue lag, and missing lifecycle timestamps by service/severity.

component.highlightReason: Operational goals require measured lifecycle events, not dashboard estimates.

steps.title: Stream lifecycle events to analytics
steps.content: Send immutable incident transition events with timestamps and service IDs; deduplicate by transition ID so replay does not distort MTTD, MTTA, or MTTR.

connection.label: Lifecycle and SLO events
connection.description: Deduplicated first-signal, detection, page, acknowledgement, and verified-resolution events.

steps.title: Add automatic post-incident reporting
steps.content: On verified resolution, assemble a draft timeline, impact, owner and escalation history, actions, outcome, and links to evidence. Mark unknown cause and unresolved follow-ups honestly; let the incident owner review before distribution.

component.label: Post-Incident Report Builder

properties.purpose: Generate a draft report from verified incident events, impact, timeline, ownership, actions, outcome, and source links; mark unknowns and require owner review before distribution.

component.highlightReason: A generated report should be traceable to the authoritative incident timeline.

steps.title: Trigger reports after verified resolution
steps.content: Consume an idempotent verified-resolution event; do not generate final reports for transient auto-closed candidates.

connection.label: Verified resolution trigger
connection.description: Deduplicated closure event with metrics and report job ID.

steps.title: Read authoritative incident evidence
steps.content: Fetch versioned timeline and approvals from the incident store; missing evidence appears as an explicit report gap rather than a guessed root cause.

connection.label: Timeline and outcome
connection.description: Versioned incident events, owner handoffs, actions, and verified resolution evidence.

steps.title: Add durable report storage
steps.content: Store versioned draft and reviewed reports with checksums, retention, tenant access controls, and immutable source links; do not include secrets or raw sensitive telemetry by default.

component.label: Post-Incident Report Archive

properties.purpose: Store versioned draft and reviewed incident reports with tenant-scoped access, checksum validation, retention, and source references.

component.highlightReason: Reports must survive worker retries and remain reviewable after an incident closes.

steps.title: Write versioned reports
steps.content: Use the incident ID and report version as an idempotent object key; distribute only a reviewed version through authorized channels.

connection.label: Draft and reviewed report
connection.description: Checksum-validated, versioned report artifact keyed by incident and revision.

steps.title: Add reviewed learning pipeline
steps.content: Build labeled examples from resolved incidents only after responder review. Compare new detection and correlation models with the held-out set, including false merges and service segments; canary and roll back a release that degrades the brief's detection, correlation, or noise targets.

component.label: Incident Feedback and Training
component.description: Reviewed outcomes and gated model versions

properties.purpose: Curate human-reviewed incident labels and rejected suggestions; evaluate detection latency, correlation accuracy above 90%, false merges, and 80% noise reduction before canary promotion or rollback.

component.highlightReason: Learning needs verified outcomes and a release gate, not automatic self-reinforcement.

steps.title: Feed reviewed incidents into training
steps.content: Extract consented, tenant-isolated, versioned outcomes and negative examples; exclude unreviewed reports and redact secrets before feature construction.

connection.label: Reviewed labels
connection.description: Versioned incident outcomes, false merges, rejected suggestions, and redacted features.

steps.title: Promote gated model versions
steps.content: Deploy a canary model only after offline incident-level validation, shadow comparison, and rollback readiness; record model version on every new grouping.

connection.label: Validated model version
connection.description: Reviewed-label evaluation, canary promotion, drift monitoring, and rollback.

steps.title: Choose reviewed feedback over self-training
steps.content: Use reviewed resolution and false-merge labels, hold out incidents by time and service, and promote a candidate only when detection, correlation, and noise metrics meet the frozen targets. Monitor post-deploy drift and roll back bad versions.

decision.question: When may incident history change the active correlation model?
decision.chosen: After human review, temporal holdout validation, canary, and rollback readiness
decision.chosenReason: Unreviewed incident outcomes and automatic retraining can amplify earlier false correlations.

alternatives.option: Train immediately on every auto-closed incident
alternatives.tradeoff: Feeds model errors back as false ground truth.
Prevents learning as services and alert distributions change.

properties.purpose: Use human-reviewed resolved cases and false-merge labels; validate by time and service against two-minute detection, above-90% correlation accuracy, and 80% noise reduction targets; canary, monitor drift, and roll back degradations.

steps.title: Review the complete design against the brief
steps.content: Replay all applied component, connection, and decision actions, then inspect the graph for disconnected roles and missing audit paths. The review must verify the stated targets: detection within 2 minutes, correlation accuracy above 90%, 10k+ alerts per hour, 80% noise reduction without suppressing distinct critical incidents, and a dependency graph supporting 100+ microservices. Test burst and replay behavior as resilience scenarios, not as additional numeric brief requirements. Verify MTTD/MTTA/MTTR and report generation from real lifecycle events. This local draft makes those targets explicit but does not prove live performance or assessment quality.
